channel.title: Daily World Bulletin

item.title: Jharkhand CM Vows Action As Exam Protests Continue
item.description: Jharkhand Chief Minister has assured justice for protesting youth, stating that strict action will be taken against those found guilty of irregularities in examinations. Following discussions with the state government, student representatives announced that their protests would continue. A government panel also met a protester on a hunger strike to urge him to end his fast. Meanwhile, participants maintained that future opportunities for the youth must be protected, as demonstrations and talks unfold across the state.

item.title: Israel Rejects Trump's Gaza Plan Unless Hamas Disarms
item.description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has turned down a proposed 15-point peace plan for Gaza, stating clearly that the nation's military forces will not withdraw from the territory until Hamas is thoroughly and genuinely disarmed. This rejection highlights the ongoing deadlock in negotiations and underlines Israel's strict security conditions for ending the current conflict in the region, according to the latest reports from international broadcasters.

item.title: India Needs 37 Runs to Win Tour Match Against Sri Lanka XI
item.description: During the tour match day three updates against Sri Lanka XI, India reached 170 for three wickets and required 37 more runs for victory. Jadeja was at the crease as the innings progressed. Earlier, Devdutt Padikkal made a strong claim for the number three position by scoring 142 runs, which highlighted India's batting response. Openers Shubman Gill and Yashasvi Jaiswal also helped keep the target chase on track with a solid start during the warm-up fixture, bringing positive takeaways for the team.

item.title: Kiara Advani Attends Toxic Trailer Launch in All-White Outfit
item.description: Actor Kiara Advani recently made headlines at the trailer launch event for the upcoming film Toxic, wearing an all-white ensemble featuring a corset top and a thigh-slit skirt. item.title: Delhi sees significant rise in H1N1 and dengue cases
item.description: Delhi has witnessed a sharp six-fold increase in H1N1 influenza cases alongside a surge in dengue infections during the monsoon season. Hospitals report a twenty to thirty percent rise in viral fever and respiratory patients, with some COVID-19 cases turning moderately severe. Medical professionals note that swine flu is triggering more intensive care admissions, compounded by public complacency regarding flu vaccinations. Doctors have urged residents not to ignore warning signs as viral illnesses continue to spread across the capital region.

According to reports, stones and shoes were thrown at her vehicle, and mud was smeared on the cars during the visit. The Chief Minister stated that she could have died in the incident. Meanwhile, she also faced protests from locals during her travel to the residence of the deceased party worker. Further details regarding the security breach are awaited.

Meanwhile, Shahnavaz Khan added to India's success by bagging a bronze medal in the long jump. These outstanding performances helped India equal its best-ever medal tally at the prestigious global under-20 athletics competition, marking a memorable night for Indian athletics on the international stage.
